Runs: E2 configurations with --sync-timers 1 and 100 fixed iterations (E2: 200), so the labels (t_iter of these runs) differ from F4 / T2. t_wait is a timed MPI_Barrier before each of the 2 Allreduces per iteration (standard CG). Inside one node a barrier costs µs, so t_wait is the waiting for the slowest rank (load imbalance); the Allreduce itself then costs 2 – 40 µs per iteration. Across nodes the barrier itself costs about as much as an Allreduce (0.2 – 0.4 ms per iteration at p = 256 / 288), so there t_wait is waiting plus synchronisation. The barriers make t_iter ≤ 2 % longer on 1 node (about 0.5 % of it is the shorter run: the initial residual is spread over 100 instead of 200 iterations); on 4 nodes 3D −1 / +2 %, 2D +6 / +13 % (+0.2 / +0.4 ms). These runs are used for the breakdown only, not for speedups. Boundary fill = physical (Dirichlet) ghost layers, also present at p = 1; it shrinks with the local box and is done only by ranks at the domain boundary.

## E4 — halo exchange: measured vs message-time model (per CG iteration)

Model (a lower estimate): per decomposed dimension two message times (two blocking Sendrecv calls, also when the dimension has only 2 processes), each the measured one-way ping-pong time at the face size r·(face area)·8 B, largest local box; no contention for the network card or memory bandwidth (64 – 72 ranks per node share them). 'inter-node' assumes that every face crosses nodes: with 72 ranks per node only part of them do, so it is not an upper bound. The measured value is t_halo − t_bc (boundary fill removed); it still contains the packing of non-contiguous faces (MPI derived datatypes) and waiting for the neighbours. At p = 1 (no messages) it is 0.001 ms (3D) and 0.001 ms (2D) per iteration.
